records.subagent_summary: All 8 public rollouts scored 0 (execution 149.158): every one opened separate global sum and product cases and judged uncertainty from the public number alone ("many pairs sum to 2002"), then flipped to "but he can just subtract/divide", called the puzzle contradictory, and boxed an arbitrary factor 143 (four times) or burned the 16k cap looping (four hit finish_reason=length). The revision replaces the incumbent's abstract joint-recount language with the concrete step the failures skipped, indexing every knowledge judgement by the speaker's own private value with the unstated structural choice carried inside each scenario, and it is deliberately shorter because in this hint's history longer, more problem-specific hints have consistently transferred worse.

All 8 round-8 rollouts scored 1, so training is saturated and the loss is transfer and token waste: every rollout reached the modulus ratio within the first 5-17% of its text, yet 6 of 8 then spent the middle half of the response re-deriving individual roots as exponentials (7-27 e^{...} expressions each), and the two longest (5.9k and 6.0k tokens, 12-14 hedges) opened by taking a 6th root of the equation itself before recovering. The clearest self-inflicted stall came from a rollout that tested the center point against the locus equation, found it failed, and questioned the whole circle. The revision therefore states the modulus/argument division of labour so enumeration is visibly unnecessary rather than merely forbidden, keeps the moduli-before-exponents ordering, and replaces the incumbent's vague verification advice with a concrete rule that spot-checks use a point at the radius, not the center, which never satisfies the locus.

Training scored 5/8; all three failures ran out the 16384-token cap rather than committing a wrong answer, and each died in the same place: reasoning about the large square's center-to-side distance as if the shared point were its center, concluding from that distance and from size that the small square must lie wholly inside, then oscillating between that claim and an unclosed tangency search. One failure had already computed the correct aligned overlap and then abandoned it after the distance argument contradicted it. The revision makes the wedge concrete by putting the axes on the corner's own edges so uncovered points are exactly those with a negative coordinate, names the center-vs-corner confusion as the specific fallacy, and closes with an explicit stop that forbids the angle/tangency retesting loop.

My 8 public rollouts with the incumbent scored 7/8; the lone failure terminated normally rather than truncating, and it failed by never partitioning indices at all: it chained adjacent board entries into P_{i+1}(i+1) - P_i(i) = d, concluded each function may be used only once, and reported N as the count. Rounds 3-7 showed that rewriting or piling reject-rules onto the incumbent collapses train, while round 6's extremal reframe was the only variant to raise heldout, so this revision keeps the incumbent's proven skeleton verbatim and adds only the portable bound-meets-construction opener plus a four-word note that the root cap is per group so N alone is not the count.

All 8 public rollouts were correct this round, so train is saturated and only transfer binds (heldout 0.1375 for the incumbent). The one clearly defective trace was also the longest (13360 tokens): it restated the single vector equality as equal diagonal midpoints, copied the y-gap as 3 instead of 1, and ground out an irrational quadratic before backtracking. Round 6's best-ever heldout (0.1625) came from the free-root idea, so this revision keeps the incumbent's proven pipeline, bans the midpoint restatement, and states the degenerate-root test as a one-shot validity check plus a factoring shortcut instead of a redo-loop instruction.

All 8 rollouts scored 0: seven explicitly asserted the final order is a uniformly random permutation and answered 1/n (six gave 1/4 or 1/2 for part b, one gave 1/24), and several miscounted the process as n moves with n binary choices (hence 1/2^(n-1) or 1/16) instead of 2n carries. The incumbent already bans symmetry claims and gives the orientation rule, so this revision adds the two structural facts the failures actually lacked: the random draw is over direction only while the item moved is forced by the stack top, and each item is carried twice so the move count is 2n.

My 8 rollouts scored 1/8, and the single success came purely from solving n=2,3,4 by elimination and fitting a signed-factorial pattern, never from the incumbent's functional/Lagrange framing; two other rollouts reached the same numeric ladder but mis-fit the closed form (off-by-one factorial, or 1/2005!), and the rest burned the 16384-token cap on Vandermonde-inverse or interpolation detours after mis-scaling a toy with more conditions than unknowns and calling it inconsistent. Seven prior rounds of functional/test-polynomial rewordings all lost heldout accuracy, so this proposal switches register entirely to the mechanism that demonstrably produced the win: a correctly-scaled small-case ladder plus an explicit refit-and-verify step against every toy value.

6/8 public rollouts were correct; both failures shared the known mode, silently equating the stated group count with the unit count, confirming divisibility, and never invoking gcd or maximality at all. Rounds 5, 6 and 7 each attacked exactly that mode with more divisibility apparatus (front-loaded warning, maximality certificate, quantity-labelling) and every one raised train while collapsing heldout from 0.2125 to 0.1125, 0.0625 and 0.125, so with lambda=5 adding more anti-substitution machinery is a demonstrated loss. I therefore left the incumbent's spine and ordering untouched and spent the budget on dead weight instead: no correct rollout ever used the 'scaling and dividing commute' clause, so I replaced it with a portable percentage-base discipline (markup on cost multiplies by 1+p, whereas a percentage of the selling price or final total requires division), which is a distinct and common failure source on unseen percent word problems.

All 8 public rollouts were correct again (8/8, 3.1k-6.5k tokens, none truncated), so the training question stays saturated and every remaining point is transfer. The uniform new waste is that once the centered ansatz is substituted the composition identity becomes a tautology, and rollouts misread this as the constraints being insufficient: they relitigate uniqueness (3-6 'unique' passes each) and one spends ~2k tokens arguing the family is underdetermined with infinitely many solutions before recovering. This revision keeps the proven trigger, centered ansatz, factored both-branch condition, symmetric-combination rule and verification spine and adds only a portable closure rule - an auto-satisfied identity is expected, so compare the family's free parameters to the independent given conditions instead of doubting uniqueness.

Only 2/8 rollouts were correct; three failures that terminated all answered 2 by asserting one switcheroo is a product of disjoint transpositions (they literally wrote block-swap cycle products with non-overlapping index sets) and never applied the full loop twice to check, while another mislabelled each sub-step as a separate application before drifting to a different closed form. The revision adds a cheap structural falsifier the incumbent lacks -- write down the index set each sub-step touches and observe they share indices, so the composite cannot be independent swaps of order 2 -- and reinforces the application boundary by recording state only after each complete loop.
